story: The demon Raktabija could create a copy of himself from every drop of his blood that touched the ground. Kali burst from Durga's brow and drank every drop before it fell. Her victory dance grew so wild that Shiva lay down in her path, and she stopped only when she stepped on him.
belief: Kali is the goddess of time, change and death, who destroys ego and fear. In Bengal and Assam she is loved as a mother, and saints like Ramakrishna saw her as the most tender form of the divine.
turns: Her fury once went beyond its purpose and threatened the very world she was saving. The famous image of her tongue out, one foot on Shiva, is often read as the moment she realised it and stopped.
facts: Kali Puja falls on the same night as Diwali in Bengal.
Kalighat and Dakshineswar in Kolkata are famous Kali temples.
Her name comes from kala, which means both 'time' and 'black'.
lessons: Face your fear and it shrinks.
Know when your anger has done its work.
Letting go of ego is a kind of freedom.
more: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa served as a priest at the Dakshineswar Kali temple.
Kalighat is counted among the Shakti Peethas, the shrines where parts of Sati's body are said to have fallen.
